messages.subject: Microclimate estimates on islands
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I've been following the development of the micro climate model in R for some time- it's great to be able to use it. I have a small query that I hope someone can help me with :)

I have latlong coordinates from a raster at 1km2 (the centroids of each 1km2 cell in the raster). I'd like to calculate microclimate at each of these points to generate a microclimate surface. These microclimate estimates will, eventually, find their way into the ectotherm model for the lizards I'm currently studying (Anolis) so that I can attempt to approximate the fundamental niche of some species across islands. I believe the approach of running the microclimate and ectotherm models for each point across the landscape is the way to do this but please correct me if I'm wrong.

I've made sure that my 1km2 map of Jamaica is the same extent and CRS as the global climate database that NicheMapR uses (CRU climate data). However, there are many points that fall outside the extent of the global climate surface and so I get the error:

extracting climate data
extracting soil moisture data
Sorry, there is no environmental data for this location

If I plot the point in question, it does indeed fall outside the global climate surface at ~17km2, despite being on dry land at 1km2.

I have uploaded an image so you can see what I mean. The coloured cells are from the global climate surface that's downloaded when using NicheMapR. The small circles are the centre points of each cell on the island at 1km2. While most of the points are absolutely fine and overlap the global climate layer, there are many that don't and so I can't estimate climate for these points.

I was wondering if there's anything I can do to resolve this, or is it a limitation of the CRUs climate data? It seems that coastal areas could be problematic which is a shame as I study lizards on islands!

messages.subject: Re: Microclimate estimates on islands
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

Sorry, that's the extent of the CRU data. What you could do is take the mean air temperatures from the coarse grid and adjust them for the elevation effect - the lapse rate. You get the elevation for a given pixel from the coarse grid, find the difference between this elevation and that of each of your fine-resolution pixels within it, and then multiply the differences by the lapse rate. A typical lapse rate is 1 degree per 100 m, but you should ideally look to see if it has been measured for your site as it can vary a lot, in part due to humidity. Note you should also adjust the relative humidity of the pixel to the new temperature, which you can do with the 'wetair' function in NicheMapR.

All the best,
Mike
